Closing it either narrows ADR-0048 §3.3 for bucket 1 (option A: a bare read refuses with 409 when two or more packages hold the name) or reverses ADR-0150 D1 (option B). Option C closes it as by design. The question is with the maintainer. Correction to the card body: Clause-② reads `no (narrowing)`, not "yes, narrowing". Whoever records the ruling removes needs-user-decision and restores pm:queue (or closes).

domain:server#5 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jRsWwTRkuRCyQwvpAG

Ruled: option A · the maintainer (Steedos) on the seat thread decision card (2026-11-15T11:23Z), answering the analysis 6893232800 after an independent Fable review. Chosen option, verbatim as the card read: 「A 拒绝并列出候选」 (a bare read refuses and lists the holders).

Ruling as it binds this card:
- A context-free read of a `doc` name held by two or more enabled packages answers 409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT naming every holder. With one holder, nothing changes. `doc` stays in ADR-0150 D1 bucket 1 (global literal name, addressing unchanged). Exact-address reads, own-package-first and `?package=` reads are unchanged. A disabled package is not a holder, and the environment's own saved row still answers first (the action precedent, protocol-meta-item-reads.ts).
- The refusal covers both the REST door and the in-process facade (`metadata-facade` get('doc', name) through `registry.resolveItem`/`getItem`), not the REST door alone.
- This aligns reads with ADR-0146 D8 and with the bare save/delete/publish/layered-read doors, which already refuse 409 (sys-metadata-repository.ts). The ADR-0048 status line drops its "packages with no dependency keep the old sentence" carve-out for `doc`. That is a docs/adr/** status-line edit, carried by a domain:skills card.
- Clause-②: narrowing (the bare read moves from an answer to a refusal). Contract review on the narrowing face owed. The Console `/docs/<name>` route must show the candidate packages on a 409: a UI-lane follow-up.

State: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` (area S5 claims; lease E1).
